lifecycle.origin: Created 2026-08-16 by KERNEL_BUILDER from the measured breakage of the operator-directed physical PostgreSQL removal, so the remaining migration work is tracked and not lost.

landed: process_ledger/writer.rs: PostgresProcessLedgerStore -> SurrealProcessLedgerStore over the kernel_process_lifecycle table. The two ON CONFLICT update lists were reproduced field-for-field in Rust: START coalesces optional identity columns and takes the earliest started_at but never touches stopped_at/exit_code/stop_reason, so a replayed START cannot erase a STOP that already landed; STOP overwrites only the stop triple. Both merges stay idempotent, so the existing retain-and-retry loop re-converges.

session_checkpoint/writer.rs: append-only writes keyed on checkpoint_id. An existing id is skipped and NOT counted in the returned row count, reproducing ON CONFLICT (checkpoint_id) DO NOTHING plus rows_affected, so an idempotent retry neither errors nor double-counts.

flight_recorder/fr_emitter.rs: batch flusher appends kernel_event_ledger through the embedded store. Ledger ordering stays owned by the database via event_sequence DEFAULT sequence::nextval. A real regression was prevented: the old batch was one transaction, so a mid-batch failure rolled back and the retained batch replayed each event exactly once; with per-record commits the flusher now drains the successfully-written prefix before propagating the error, restoring exactly-once.
process_ledger/table.rs: deleted the three PostgreSQL DDL/DML constants as dead residue.
progress_2026_08_16.known_regression_disclosed: Batch atomicity is lost in the process ledger: rows now commit individually rather than as one transaction. The merges are idempotent so recovery still converges, but this is a real semantic change and is recorded rather than hidden.
progress_2026_08_16.deliberate_non_regression: process_ledger/reclaim.rs went 4 -> 5 errors ON PURPOSE. Its store no longer has a PgPool, and reclaim depends on an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE stopped_at IS NULL ... RETURNING whose lock covers the kill-and-STOP decision. Emulating that with read-then-write would be a silent correctness regression, so the honest compile error was left in place.
still_blocked_on: Schema coverage: user_manual_* (7 tables), knowledge_ingestion_* (6) and knowledge_agent_* (6) do not exist in schema.surql. A dedicated schema lane is adding them.

The deleted crate::storage::postgres module is still imported by user_manual/{store,seed,freshness,fixtures,bundle_bridge}.rs and knowledge_ingestion/engine.rs, which need the SurrealDatabase equivalent plus an in-transaction ledger-append helper.
progress_2026_08_16.unblocked_since: The SurrealDataContext seam has been widened by the KERNEL_BUILDER since this pass and now provides bound queries, delete, and an atomic create_if_absent that replaces the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus SQLSTATE 23505 pattern. Transaction scope is available by writing BEGIN TRANSACTION; ...; COMMIT TRANSACTION; as a single statement through query_values.
progress_2026_08_16.proofs_not_run: PT-137-2 and PT-137-3 could not execute: handshake_core does not compile as a whole, so no test binary can be built. AC-137-1 is NOT met - sqlx references remain in the modules that lack the schema or the ported dependencies.
progress_2026_08_16.tests_needing_their_own_mt: tests/process_ledger_tests.rs, tests/process_ledger_reclaim_tests.rs, tests/focus_audit_tests.rs and tests/hbr_e2e_smoke_test.rs assert on the deleted PostgreSQL DDL constants and call apply_migration(). Those assertions cannot survive the pivot and need their own microtask.

scope.summary: Port the non-storage backend infrastructure off sqlx: swarm_orchestration/state_recovery.rs (60), user_manual/store.rs (48), process_ledger (48), role_mailbox_v1 (34), mt_executor (32), knowledge_ingestion (32), flight_recorder (29), knowledge_memory (20), kernel (18), knowledge_retrieval (13) and session_checkpoint (7). These own process and session lifecycle, the role mailbox, the microtask executor queue and Flight Recorder spans, so they must keep their existing durability and ordering semantics. EVIDENCE: Measured from a full cargo check of handshake_core after the physical PostgreSQL removal on 2026-08-16 (log Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp012-surreal-breakage-20260816T033259Z.log): 1716 errors across 119 files. Root causes: 1493 unresolved sqlx, 152 missing migrations .sql include_bytes (since restored), 51 deleted-postgres-module references, 20 other. SEAM: The Database trait has 201 methods: 108 required and 93 with default bodies (88 of those return StorageError::NotImplemented and 5 are supports_ capability flags). storage/surreal/database.rs already implements all 108 required methods and compiles clean; 106 currently return NotImplemented. storage/surreal/schema.surql already defines 121 tables, 1414 fields and 347 indexes, and storage/surreal/documents.rs, blocks.rs, workspaces.rs and preferences.rs already implement 36 working functions - use those as the implementation pattern. Decrement DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED in database.rs in the SAME change that ports each method; the not_implemented_surface_is_declared test enforces it.

acceptance_criteria.text: None of these modules references sqlx.
Process-ledger and session-checkpoint durability and restart-recovery semantics are preserved and proven across a store reopen.
Flight Recorder append and query behaviour is unchanged from the consumer side.

proof_targets: PT-137-1: cargo check output showing zero sqlx errors in these modules.
PT-137-2: a restart-recovery proof against a real embedded store showing state survives a process restart.
PT-137-3: a Flight Recorder append-then-read proof against the real store.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend storage port with no operator-visible surface of its own; the surfaces it restores are proven by their own microtasks.

target_entries: process, session and Flight Recorder persistence behaviour after the port

risks: Losing ordering or idempotency in the process ledger would corrupt restart recovery.
Flight Recorder is the Tier 1 diagnostic ledger; weakening it silently removes observability.
minimum_controls: No method may be left returning NotImplemented while any microtask claims that behaviour works.
Every ported method needs a proof that touches a real embedded SurrealDB store, never a mock.
DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED must be decremented in the same change that ports a method.
